data.body:
LIVE TIER RAN IN CI (GitHub Actions run 30604756524, job 'jira DC harness smoke') — and it FOUND A
REAL DEFECT. Result: 2 failed, 12 passed, 1 error.

THE HEADLINE: a WRITING reconcile pass against a real Jira DC instance CRASHES.

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

dry-run passes (test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception is green); only the writing path
dies. Filed as [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5].

ROOT CAUSE, which is the interesting part: set_entity_property is called from THREE core sites
(dispatch_one.py:321, binding_store.py:517, apply_inbound_records.py:279), implemented in exactly ONE
(adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:266, Cloud) — and is NOT A MEMBER OF THE TicketTransport PROTOCOL, which
declares only create_issue / get_issue / update_issue / transition_issue_by_name / add_label /
search_issues. The core depends on a transport method the port never states.

That is why everything in this story passed while the real thing was broken: isinstance(x,
TicketTransport) is satisfied without it, the contract suite never calls it, and 1636 unit tests are
green. Making the DC backend Backend-conformant — this story's core work — was NECESSARY BUT NOT
SUFFICIENT, because the Protocol is not a faithful statement of what the core requires. Conformance to
an incomplete port proves less than it appears to. Same class as J6's add_label defect.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS STORY'S ACs — the three [operator-attested] live criteria are NOT met, and I am
not marking them met:
  * full reconcile pass converges + repeated pass writes nothing -> FAILED (exit 1)
  * DC-created ticket provenance                                 -> FAILED (same crash)
  * zero unhandled exceptions                                    -> PASSED for dry-run ONLY
The epic cannot honestly claim 'Jira Server/Data Center support' while a DC deployment cannot complete
a writing pass.

SECOND FINDING, and MY tests caused it: [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8]. The run also errored at SETUP of
an unrelated, previously-passing test with 'UserTokenLimitExceededException: You can't create more
than 10 tokens'. jira_dc_pat (conftest.py:355) is FUNCTION-scoped with no teardown, so every consuming
test mints a new PAT and never deletes it; Jira DC caps a user at 10. My three new tests transitively
request it and pushed the session past the cap. The bug was latent; my tests made it fire — and it
surfaces in a module nobody touched, which is exactly the misattribution that burns a session.

WHAT WENT RIGHT: this is the live tier doing precisely its job. Every unit-level signal was green; only
driving a real instance exposed it. That is the whole argument for this story carrying a live AC — and
it vindicates not closing on the unit evidence alone.
